newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Boots set for solid first half.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Boots set for solid first half.

text.p: The prospect of a free-for-all in Britain in over-the-counter drugs and vitamin pills could take the some of the gloss off solid first half results from Boots Co Plc when it reports next Thursday.
But the group's success in fending off price competition in the past proves that worries about a drug price war are overdone, retail analysts said.

Analysts predicted Britain's biggest chemist will raise pretax profits to between 225 and 241 million stg versus 218.7 million in last year's first half. Boots is expected to declare a dividend of about 6.2 pence up from 5.7p a year earlier.

Boots shares dipped last week when Britain's Office of Fair Trading announced a move to end recommended retail prices on over-the-counter medicines and dietary supplements. But analysts said reaction was overdone and Boots had the muscle to withstand a price battle with retailing rivals, which increasingly include superstores such as Tesco Plc and ASDA Group.
"Boots has shown great skills in the past in combating price competition, so we don't have any major fears about it," said one retail analyst, who asked to remain anonymous.
Boots the Chemist is expected to keep up its record of strong growth, but a cooler summer might have affected sun cream sales, which did well in 1995.

Analysts see an improved performance from car accessory chain Halfords and reduced losses at home decorating stores A.G. Stanley. But losses at Do It All will have increased as Boots is now the sole owner, after buying out joint venture partner W.H. Smith Group Plc.
Analysts expect a loss from Do It All of six million stg against a loss of 4.8 million last time.
But the more buoyant consumer climate and recovery in the housing market will have helped DIY sales.
"The sales trends in those businesses will be very much better than we have seen last year," said another analyst.
Analysts said results from Boots Healthcare International were difficult to call, because of uncertainties about costs and investment.
They welcomed Boots' recently announced move into continental Europe and the Far East, saying this made sense given the group's lack of success in expanding outside the Boots retail brand in Britain.
In July Boots said total group sales were ahead by 7.2 percent in the first quarter, which lagged some other retailers which were seeing double digit growth.
Analysts believe overall sales will have improved since then, but maybe not by enough to prompt profit upgrades.
